title: Graphics in U sixty-four BBC BASIC.
shapes: All of the BBC Micro's graphics are there, in the BBC's coordinates, with every shape of the BBC Master and the graphics extension ROM: lines, circles, ellipses, triangles and rectangles, outlined or filled, and pattern fills.
modes: Here the same test card in mode one, two, four and five: four, sixteen, two and four colours.
upiclite: On a sixty-four megahertz Ultimate, these modes are drawn as U-pic Lite: two hundred and fifty-six lines with square pixels, as on a BBC. This is Eric Schraf's Bubble Universe, which came here by way of Arch Bas on the Archimedes.
c64: The Commodore's own modes are there as well: the text screen, hires and multicolour, with the VIC-II's colour rules.
ttx: Mode seven is teletext, with its mosaic graphics and double height.
race: The star graphics commands are fast: hundreds of filled circles and triangles in eight seconds, from BASIC.
upicfull: Mode one ten is U-pic full: three hundred and eighty-four by two hundred and fifty-six, every pixel its own colour, kept in the R E U.
tables: Fast integer tables make a rotating cube, spirographs and a plasma possible in plain BASIC. The plasma moves by changing the palette only.
sprites: Thirty-two sprites, multiplexed, from BASIC. Enough for a game.
sedit: With a sprite editor built in: here a shape in multicolour, drawn, filled and flipped.
map: CharPad maps load and scroll with one command. This landscape was made for this video.
petscii: And for PETSCII art: a full PETSCII mode, with the C sixty-four's graphics keys.
credits: U sixty-four BBC BASIC is free and open source. Find it on GitHub. The next video is about sound and music.
